subject: [RFC PATCH v2 05/18] mm: expedite the grace period when a CPU has many deferred frees

2026-11-04.patch_summary: This patch aims to improve the performance of deferred frees in the Linux kernel by introducing an expedited grace period when a CPU has many pending folios (memory allocations). When more than 4 MiB is pending on a CPU, the patch takes both lists and frees them after an expedited grace period. This approach ensures that memory is freed quickly when it's needed, without waiting for the normal grace period. The patch also introduces a new counter in /proc/vmstat to track the number of times this expedited process has freed memory. The goal is to prevent memory bottlenecks and improve system responsiveness, especially during bulk frees triggered by operations like file truncation or fadvise(POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED).
